must make the gate go red. One that escapes is a class of bug that can currently
merge into DynaChat with nobody reading the diff.
This is the ONLY thing in the gate that measures the HARNESS rather than the code.
Until one of these has been injected and caught there is no evidence any check here
THIS FILE IS PROTECTED. A builder that can edit its own defect set can pass it.

All four aim at MISSION hard invariants 1 and 2, which are the two the factory is
least able to recover from getting wrong and the two issue #361 turned on.
_written: 2026-08-13, at the same time as the holdout. See .factory/holdout/run.py for why that date is stated rather than buried.

defects.why: MISSION hard invariant 1 is a specific number, not 'there is a limit'. A cap silently raised 4x still rate-limits, still passes every test that asserts a limit exists, and quietly quadruples the OpenRouter bill this invariant was written to protect.

An output made constant. Every user now serialises on ONE advisory lock: the limiter still works for a single user and still passes its unit tests, but under concurrency unrelated users block each other, and a shared lock is one refactor away from a shared COUNT.
defects._why_this_shape: `% 1` rather than `= 0` ON PURPOSE. The obvious mutation leaves `hi` and `lo` unused, so ruff flags it and STATIC catches a defect that was meant to probe the holdout. This version still reads both halves and still type-checks, so it is invisible to every rung below the independence line - which is the only way this defect measures the thing it was written to measure.

defects.why: The two entry points accept UUID | str and normalise before deriving the lock key. Drop it on one path and that path locks under a different key from the other, so the two stop serialising and the effective cap doubles. Invisible to either function's own test.

defects.why: A guard removed. MISSION hard invariant 2 - authentication required for all chat access. The route still returns data, the app still boots, and every OTHER auth test still passes, because they each call a route they already know about. Only a check that walks the assembled app can see a route that lost its dependency.
